results.fact: Line followed above the notch (south ridge vs corkscrew/north ridge)
results.evidence: Sources describe two genuinely different lines: one party followed a ridge to the notch south of Degenhardt (the upper Barrier crossing) and on to a 4th-class summit, matching climbing_route; another followed a ledge behind the north skyline from the Terror-Degenhardt ridge; a third did the Corkscrew (N ridge slot, W ridge face, S ridge ledge). Which line this row's 'Southwest Route' is cannot be settled; a guidebook-level route description naming the Southwest Route would settle it.

Three independent reports call the summit 4th class (a 2014 report of the notch-south line, a 2020 report with 'a few class 4 moves', a 2021 party that hit low fifth only after missing a gully), but an NPS ranger report calls it a short class 5 climb and the Corkscrew report rates a class 4-5 face. Sources genuinely split, and the 5.6 rating is woven through grade, rock_grade, gear, pitch_detail, waypoints, pro_tips, watch_out and partner skills, so no partial change is made. A guidebook rating for this specific line would settle it.
